classification.difficultyReason: Recover roots from pairwise products, preserve the two consistent sign choices, and distinguish the two resulting coefficient sets.

content.prompt: The cubic polynomial $x^3+px^2+qx+r$ has roots $\alpha$, $\beta$ and $\gamma$ which satisfy the relationships $\alpha\beta=2$, $\beta\gamma=3$ and $\gamma\alpha=4$. Find the values of $p$, $q$ and $r$.

answer.short:
$(p,q,r)=\left(-\frac{13\sqrt6}{6},11,-2\sqrt6\right)$ or $\left(\frac{13\sqrt6}{6},11,2\sqrt6\right)$.

The pairwise products determine the root magnitudes, but allow all three roots to be positive or all three to be negative.
answer.worked:
Since all three pairwise products are positive, the roots have the same sign. Let $\varepsilon=1$ or $-1$.
$$\begin{align*}\alpha^2&=\frac{(\alpha\beta)(\alpha\gamma)}{\beta\gamma}\\\alpha^2&=\frac{2\cdot4}{3}=\frac83\\\alpha&=\varepsilon\frac{2\sqrt6}{3}\\\beta&=\frac2\alpha=\varepsilon\frac{\sqrt6}{2}\\\gamma&=\frac4\alpha=\varepsilon\sqrt6.\end{align*}$$
Apply the monic cubic relationships:
$$\begin{align*}p&=-(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)\\p&=-\varepsilon\left(\frac{2\sqrt6}{3}+\frac{\sqrt6}{2}+\sqrt6\right)\\p&=-\varepsilon\frac{13\sqrt6}{6}\\q&=\alpha\beta+\alpha\gamma+\beta\gamma\\q&=2+4+3=11\\r&=-\alpha\beta\gamma\\r&=-(\alpha\beta)\gamma\\r&=-\varepsilon2\sqrt6.\end{align*}$$
Thus $(p,q,r)=\left(-\frac{13\sqrt6}{6},11,-2\sqrt6\right)$ or $\left(\frac{13\sqrt6}{6},11,2\sqrt6\right)$.
